mentalModelCheck.question: Why does the BEAM virtual machine preempt processes after 4,000 reductions rather than relying on cooperative multitasking?

options.label: To reduce the total RAM required by operating system thread stacks
options.explanation: Stack size is determined by the BEAM process memory model (~309 words), not the reduction counter.

options.label: To prevent compute-heavy tasks from starving network I/O and low-latency message passing
options.explanation: Reduction counting guarantees soft real-time responsiveness. Even an infinite compute loop yields after 4,000 reductions.

options.label: Because the operating system kernel forces Erlang to sleep every 4,000 machine instructions
options.explanation: Reduction counting is handled entirely in user space by BEAM schedulers, not by OS interrupts.
